subject: Chemistry
description: Oxidation, reduction, oxidising/reducing agents, electron transfer

options.option_text: Loss of electrons (or gain of oxygen)

questions.explanation: OXIDATION = LOSS OF ELECTRONS (or addition of oxygen / loss of hydrogen / increase in oxidation state). REDUCTION = GAIN OF ELECTRONS (or loss of oxygen / gain of hydrogen / decrease in oxidation state). MNEMONIC: 'OIL RIG' — Oxidation Is Loss; Reduction Is Gain (of electrons). Or 'LEO the lion says GER' — Loss of Electrons = Oxidation; Gain of Electrons = Reduction. REDOX = simultaneous oxidation + reduction (always paired — electrons must go somewhere). EXAMPLES: rusting (Fe + O₂ → Fe₂O₃, Fe oxidised); photosynthesis (CO₂ reduced to glucose); respiration (glucose oxidised to CO₂); combustion (fuel oxidised to CO₂ + H₂O); batteries; metallurgy (ores reduced to metals).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: OXIDISING AGENT in a redox reaction is the:

options.option_text: Catalyst speeding up reaction without changing
Solvent in which reaction takes place

questions.explanation: OXIDISING AGENT (oxidant) = the species that GETS REDUCED (it gains electrons; in doing so, it OXIDISES the other species). REDUCING AGENT (reductant) = the species that GETS OXIDISED (loses electrons). Counter-intuitive at first, but logical: an oxidising agent CAUSES oxidation in something else. STRONG OXIDANTS: F₂ (most), O₂, Cl₂, KMnO₄ (purple), K₂Cr₂O₇ (orange), HNO₃, conc. H₂SO₄, O₃, H₂O₂, Fe³⁺. STRONG REDUCTANTS: alkali metals (Na, K, Cs — readily lose electron), Mg, Al, Zn, H₂, NaBH₄, LiAlH₄, sulfites. INSIGHT — strong oxidants are dangerous (corrosive, can ignite); SODIUM bursts in water due to redox + H₂ evolved.

questions.stem: RUSTING of iron is essentially a:

options.option_text: Slow oxidation reaction in moist air

questions.explanation: RUSTING = slow OXIDATION of iron in presence of OXYGEN + WATER → forms hydrated iron(III) oxide Fe₂O₃·xH₂O (red-brown rust). Fe → Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ (oxidation). O₂ + H₂O get reduced. Both moisture + O₂ needed (rust doesn't form in dry air or pure water alone). ACCELERATING factors: salt (electrolyte; coastal cars rust faster), acidic air, mechanical stress. PREVENTION: GALVANIZATION (Zn coating — Zn corrodes preferentially), PAINTING / OILING (barrier), GREASE, ALLOYING (stainless steel — Fe + Cr + Ni; Cr oxide layer is invisible + protective + self-healing), CATHODIC PROTECTION (sacrificial anode of Mg or Zn — used on ship hulls, pipelines). India loses ~3-5% of GDP annually to corrosion.

questions.stem: PHOTOSYNTHESIS by plants is essentially a:

options.option_text: Reduction of CO₂ to glucose (using H₂O as electron source)
Oxidation of glucose to CO₂ + water (option here)
Combustion of CO₂ + water to oxygen (option here)
Acid-base neutralisation of carbonic acid (option here)

questions.explanation: PHOTOSYNTHESIS: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. CO₂ (carbon at +4) is REDUCED to glucose (carbon at 0); H₂O OXIDISED to O₂ (electrons from water reduce CO₂). LIGHT energy drives this uphill reaction (CO₂ + H₂O are stable; glucose is high-energy). RESPIRATION = REVERSE: glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O + ATP (energy). Glucose oxidised → CO₂ (back to +4); O₂ reduced. INSIGHT — life on Earth is essentially a vast REDOX cycle: photosynthesis (plants store sun energy by reducing CO₂); respiration (animals release energy by oxidising glucose). NET CYCLE: solar energy → biomass → metabolic energy. Roughly 10% of solar light hitting earth's plants gets converted to biomass.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a strong OXIDISING AGENT?
questions.explanation: KMnO₄ (POTASSIUM PERMANGANATE) — strong oxidant. Mn is in +7 state (highest possible). Bright purple → reduced products are colourless / brown. USES: water purification, antiseptic, organic chemistry titrations, decoloriser. K₂Cr₂O₇ (POTASSIUM DICHROMATE) — orange; Cr +6 → +3 (green). HNO₃ — strong oxidant, esp. concentrated. ATOMIC OXYGEN, FLUORINE, OZONE — extreme oxidants. Distractor 4: H₂ is a strong REDUCING agent (often used to reduce metal oxides → metal in metallurgy). REDUCING agents: alkali metals, Mg, H₂, C (in steel-making, carbon reduces iron ore Fe₂O₃ + C → Fe + CO₂).

questions.stem: When zinc is added to copper sulphate solution, the change is:

options.option_text: Blue colour fades; Zn is oxidised, Cu deposits
No reaction occurs at all (option here)
Zinc absorbs water from solution (option here)

questions.explanation: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu. Zinc DISPLACES copper (since Zn is HIGHER in REACTIVITY SERIES than Cu). Zn oxidised (Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻); Cu²⁺ reduced (Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu). Blue (Cu²⁺) colour FADES → colourless (Zn²⁺). Cu deposits as reddish-brown layer on Zn surface. Solution becomes ZnSO₄ + Cu solid. REACTIVITY SERIES (most reactive → least): K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Pb, H, Cu, Ag, Au. ANY metal HIGHER displaces ANY metal LOWER from its salt. APPLICATIONS: extraction of metals (e.g., Cu from CuSO₄ using scrap iron), galvanic cells (Daniel cell uses Zn-Cu redox to generate current). PYQ STAPLE.

options.option_text: Reduction of stains via electron gain

questions.explanation: BLEACHING = oxidation of coloured compounds → colourless (chromophores destroyed). CHLORINE + water → HCl + HOCl (hypochlorous acid, the active oxidant). HOCl breaks down stain molecules. CHLORINE BLEACH (sodium hypochlorite NaOCl) — most common household bleach. OXYGEN BLEACH (H₂O₂, sodium percarbonate) — gentler, used for colour-safe bleaching, eco-friendly (decomposes to water + oxygen). BLEACHING POWDER = Ca(OCl)Cl. INDUSTRIAL: pulp/paper, textile, water treatment. CAUTION — never mix bleach with ammonia (forms toxic chloramine vapours) or with acids (releases Cl₂ gas). REDUCING bleaches also exist (SO₂ for wool/silk — gentler).
